# The same probe list through two clients, against the same catalogs.
# Generated by compare_clients.py from the two operation maps and the
# stored runs. Join only -- no network, and nothing measured here.

  rust        iceberg-catalog-rest 0.10.1, map read 2026-09-04
  pyiceberg   pyiceberg 0.12.0, map read 2026-09-17

  Both are subjects. `control` in this directory means the control
  catalog, Apache Polaris, and never one of the clients.

## What each client can express, by endpoint signature

  Variants are folded into the endpoint they vary: paper 1's rule, for
  paper 1's reason. A `+` is expressible, a `-` is not.

  endpoint                                                           rust  py
  GET /v1/config                                                     +     +
  GET /v1/{prefix}/namespaces                                        +     +
  GET /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}                            +     +
  HEAD /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}                           +     +
  GET /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables                     +     +
  GET /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables/{table}             +     +
  HEAD /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables/{table}            +     +
  GET /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables/{table}/credentials -     +
  GET /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/views                      -     +

  POST /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables/{table}/metrics    -     -

  POST /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/properties                -     +
  POST /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables                    +     +
  POST /v1/{prefix}/namespaces/{namespace}/tables/{table}            +     +

  ### Where pyiceberg refused, and what paper 1 saw

  pyiceberg compares each endpoint against the `endpoints` array of
  GET /v1/config before sending anything. Paper 1 sent the request
  regardless, so the two together say whether the refusal cost
  anything.

  load_credentials  [GATED, gate refuses]
      declared by the catalog   no
      paper 1, same endpoint    OK (declared: False)
      The endpoint answers; this client will not ask.

  plan_table_scan  [GATED, gate refuses]
      declared by the catalog   no
      paper 1, same endpoint    NOT_FOUND (declared: False)
      Client and catalog agree; the gate cost nothing.

## Auth, across every catalog the two papers share

  Catalog names and auth kinds only. This is the axis on which the two
  clients differ before a single probe is issued: the REST crate ships
  no request signer, so two of the seven cannot be reached through it,
  while pyiceberg mounts botocore and can. Rust reaches those two only
  by leaving the REST protocol for iceberg-catalog-glue or
  iceberg-catalog-s3tables, which is a loss of protocol uniformity
  rather than of capability.

  catalog              auth             rust       py         configured
  google-lakehouse     gcloud           static     static     yes
  aws-glue             sigv4            absent     native     yes
  aws-s3tables         sigv4            absent     native     yes
  databricks-unity     bearer_env       native     native     placeholder
  snowflake-horizon    oauth2           native     native     placeholder
  microsoft-onelake    azure_cli        static     static     yes
  apache-polaris       oauth2           native     native     yes

  reachable auth   rust 5 of 7, pyiceberg 7 of 7

  A row marked placeholder is carrying example config, so its auth
  kind is the example's and not the account's. Paper 1 measured
  databricks-unity and snowflake-horizon on credentials this
  configuration no longer holds -- Horizon in particular with a
  keypair-signed JWT sent as a bare client_secret, which is a
  different row in both clients' auth tables than the oauth2 above.

## What this comparison does not say

  Expressible is not correct. A `+` means the client can issue the
  request, not that what comes back is right.

  A run is one catalog at one moment, and only the control catalog has
  been run by both clients so far. The vendor columns are unmeasured,
  not empty.

  Both clients were pointed at the same fixture table through the same
  credentials. Where they disagree the difference is the client; where
  they agree it is not evidence that every catalog behaves this way.
